title: Hotel Monteleone New Orleans: Carousel Bar & Double Jeopardy
description: Hotel Monteleone in the French Quarter has a rotating Carousel Bar and appears in Double Jeopardy. History, literary ties and booking tips.
h1: Hotel Monteleone: the New Orleans hotel with the spinning bar
intro: In the French Quarter, Hotel Monteleone is known for a bar that slowly rotates while you drink. It is also family-run since 1886, and it has appeared on screen.
filming: In the 1999 thriller Double Jeopardy, scenes were shot in the hotel's lobby and at its front entrance. The Carousel Bar was dressed up as an Armani shop for the scene in which Ashley Judd's character picks up a dress.
facts: The Monteleone family has run the hotel for five generations, since Antonio Monteleone bought a small hotel here in 1886.
The hotel took its present name in 1908, after 300 rooms were added.
The Carousel Bar opened on September 3, 1949, and revolves once every 15 minutes.
Fiber optics added to the ceiling in 1992 create the effect of stars above the bar.
William Faulkner made a point of staying here, and later writers including Anne Rice and John Grisham have too.
visit: Grab a seat at the Carousel Bar early in the evening, before it fills up. The hotel is a short walk from Jackson Square and Bourbon Street.
